extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, journalists and stakeholders seeking an overview of BP plc
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style company profile of BP covering history, operations, environmental record, governance and controversies. Intended as an encyclopedic summary of corporate facts, targets, incidents and public criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indigenous rights ranking criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2016 study ranked companies on indigenous rights and resource extraction in the Arctic using 20 criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of criteria taken into account include "the companies' commitments to international standards, the presence of organisational units dedicated to handling indigenous rights, competent staffing, track records on indigenous issues, transparency, and procedures for consulting with indigenous peoples." The study noted it did not assess actual performance on indigenous rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net-zero_by_2050 emissions target
rubrics_metrics.description: BP set a goal to cut its greenhouse gas emissions to net-zero by 2050, seeking net-zero across its operations and the fuels the company sells, including emissions from cars, homes, and factories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details on scope and implementation were described as publicly limited. The company said it was restructuring operations into business groups (production & operations; customers & products; gas & low carbon; innovation & engineering) to meet goals and discontinued involvement with some lobbying groups. Membership in industry initiatives (e.g., Methane Guiding Principles) is cited as part of mitigation efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewables portfolio capacity targets
rubrics_metrics.description: BP set explicit capacity targets for its renewables portfolio: 20 GW by 2025 and 50 GW by 2030.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are numerical targets for installed renewable generation capacity used to measure progress in transitioning energy mix; the page notes BP operates wind and solar assets and holds stakes in projects and companies (e.g., Lightsource BP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-carbon investment commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: BP committed to increase its annual low carbon investments to $5 billion by 2030 (previously cited lower figures such as ~$500 million of annual spend).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investment amounts and year-by-year spending are used as evidence for assessing the company’s shift toward low-carbon technologies. Critics note opacity and claim spending was "insignificant" relative to fossil fuel investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned oil_and_gas production change metric
rubrics_metrics.description: BP announced a plan to drop oil and gas production by at least one million barrels per day by 2030 (a 40% reduction on 2019 levels), a plan later scrapped in October 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production volume targets (or reversals of those targets) are used to evaluate the company's commitment to decarbonisation; subsequent changes to those plans are cited as evidence of shifting priorities under shareholder pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment_of_rhetoric_and_actual_spending (greenwashing check)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether BP's public rhetoric and pledges on low-carbon transition match its actual spending and actions; critics called BP's clean-energy spending "insignificant and opaque" and accused it of greenwashing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look at proportion of total capital/exploratory budget allocated to alternative energy versus fossil fuels, transparency of spending, and whether marketing claims ('Beyond Petroleum', carbon neutrality pledges) are supported by measurable investment and operational changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due_diligence_and_transparency_in_deal-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations that BP performs adequate due diligence, avoids conflicts of interest, and provides transparency when acquiring development rights or entering commercial deals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Senegal case is cited: investigative reporting accused BP of "failure in due diligence" in dealings with Timis Corporation; BP stated it "paid what it considered a fair market value" but did not disclose valuation basis. Guidance includes documenting valuation bases, disclosing relevant information, and avoiding hiring parties with evident conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure_of_trade_association_memberships
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency requirement to disclose memberships and affiliations with trade associations, especially those with anti-climate or lobbying roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An investigation found BP failed to disclose membership in eight anti-climate trade associations. Disclosure is used to evaluate consistency with public climate commitments and to reveal possible adversarial lobbying activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory_compliance_for_air_pollution_controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with air quality regulations requiring companies to adequately inspect, maintain, repair and properly operate refinery equipment to avoid illegal releases of air pollutants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AQMD suits alleged BP/ARCO "failed to adequately inspect, maintain, repair and properly operate thousands of pieces of equipment...as required by AQMD regulations." Compliance is measured by inspection/maintenance records, operating practices, and regulatory fines/penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency_and_ambition_of_interim_emissions_targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of interim emissions reduction targets (e.g., reduction by 2030) for ambition and consistency over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes BP initially pledged a 35–40% cut by decade-end, later revising to a 20–30% reduction in 2023; such revisions are a metric for assessing commitment strength and susceptibility to shareholder/market pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation_in_industry_initiatives_to_reduce_emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership or founding status in industry initiatives (e.g., Methane Guiding Principles) intended to drive emissions reductions across the value chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is an indicator of engagement with best-practice frameworks; the page cites BP as a founding member of Methane Guiding Principles and involvement in other collaborative efforts (e.g., electrolyser projects with partners).
